title: Polyatomic ions
competency: Describe polyatomic ions and write and name compounds that contain them.

keywords.def: A charged group of atoms, like SO₄²⁻. Also called a compound ion.
An atom or group of atoms with a positive or negative charge.

en.text: A polyatomic ion is a charged group of atoms, like NH₄⁺, OH⁻, NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻ and PO₄³⁻. To write a formula, criss-cross the valences as before. Put the ion in brackets when it gets a subscript other than 1: ammonium sulfate is (NH₄)₂SO₄.

screens.title: A team of atoms
screens.ask: SO₄²⁻ has one sulfur and four oxygens with a 2− charge. Is it one ion or five ions?
opts: One ion made of a group of atoms
screens.after: The five atoms stay together and carry one charge. It is one polyatomic ion.
screens.best: One ion made of a group of atoms

screens.title: 3.2.6 Polyatomic ions
paras: Ions are atoms or groups of atoms with a positive or negative charge.
Simple ions: Cl⁻, O²⁻ and Al³⁺.
Polyatomic ions: NH₄⁺, OH⁻, NO₃⁻, SO₄²⁻ and PO₄³⁻.
A polyatomic ion, or compound ion, is a charged group of atoms.

root.label: Polyatomic ions
root.info: Charged groups of atoms. The number of charges is the valence.

screens.title: Example: ammonium sulfate
steps: Write the ions: NH₄⁺ and SO₄²⁻.
The 2 multiplies the whole NH₄, so keep the bracket: (NH₄)₂SO₄.

screens.title: Naming
paras: Name the metal or ammonium first, then the polyatomic ion.
NH₄Cl is ammonium chloride. Al₂(SO₄)₃ is aluminum sulfate. FeCl₃ is iron (III) chloride.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A charged group of atoms, like SO₄²⁻. Also called a compound ion.

screens.text: What is the formula of the nitrate ion?
screens.why:
Nitrate is in Table 3.6, valence 1.
It has one N and three O: NO₃.
Its charge is 1−: NO₃⁻.
NO₂⁻ has only two O: that is nitrite.

screens.title: Match ion and name
screens.why:
From Table 3.6:
NH₄⁺ is ammonium. OH⁻ is hydroxide.
SO₄²⁻ is sulfate. CO₃²⁻ is carbonate.
PO₄³⁻ is phosphate.
screens.text: Match each polyatomic ion to its name.
Write the formula of calcium nitrate (Ca = 2, NO₃ = 1).
screens.why:
Ions: Ca²⁺ and NO₃⁻. Valences: 2 and 1.
Criss-cross: Ca takes 1, NO₃ takes 2.
The 2 multiplies the whole NO₃ group, so use brackets.
Answer: Ca(NO₃)₂.
CaNO₆ is wrong: it breaks up the nitrate group.
screens.clue: Brackets go around the whole ion.

screens.why:
Na is sodium: it comes first.
HCO₃⁻ is in Table 3.6, valence 1.
Its name is hydrogen carbonate.
Answer: sodium hydrogen carbonate.

screens.title: Simple or polyatomic?
screens.text: Sort each ion: one atom, or a group of atoms?
screens.why:
Count the atoms in each ion.
Cl⁻, O²⁻ and Al³⁺ each have one atom: simple ions.
NH₄⁺ has 5 atoms, OH⁻ has 2, SO₄²⁻ has 5.
A charged group of atoms is a polyatomic ion.
screens.clue: Does the ion have one symbol, or several?

screens.text: List the elements: which elements are combined in ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄?
screens.why:
List every symbol in (NH₄)₂SO₄.
NH₄ gives N and H.
SO₄ gives S and O.
So four elements: N, H, S, O.
"Ammonium" is an ion, not an element.
screens.clue: List every symbol in the formula.

items.text: Write the formula of the compound of Na⁺ and nitrate (NO₃⁻).
items.why:
Valences: Na 1, NO₃ 1.
Criss-cross: Na₁(NO₃)₁.
Omit the 1s; no brackets are needed.
Answer: NaNO₃.

items.text: Write the formula of the compound of Ca²⁺ and sulfate (SO₄²⁻).
items.why:
Valences: Ca 2, SO₄ 2.
Criss-cross: Ca₂(SO₄)₂.
Both are 2: divide by 2.
Answer: CaSO₄.

items.text: Write the formula of the compound of Al³⁺ and sulfate (SO₄²⁻).
items.why:
Valences: Al 3, SO₄ 2.
Criss-cross: Al takes 2, SO₄ takes 3.
Brackets keep the SO₄ group together.
Answer: Al₂(SO₄)₃.
Check: 2 × 3 = 6 = 3 × 2.

items.text: Write the formula of the compound of NH₄⁺ and phosphate (PO₄³⁻).
items.why:
Valences: NH₄ 1, PO₄ 3.
Criss-cross: NH₄ takes 3, PO₄ takes 1.
Brackets show that 3 multiplies the whole NH₄ group.
Answer: (NH₄)₃PO₄.
Check: 3 × 1 = 3 = 1 × 3.

items.text: Write the formula of the compound of Ca²⁺ and phosphate (PO₄³⁻).
items.why:
Valences: Ca 2, PO₄ 3.
Criss-cross: Ca takes 3, PO₄ takes 2.
Brackets keep the PO₄ group together.
Answer: Ca₃(PO₄)₂.
Check: 3 × 2 = 6 = 2 × 3.

NH₄⁺ is ammonium: it comes first.
Cl is chlorine, which becomes chloride.
Answer: ammonium chloride.

Each nitrate (NO₃⁻) has valence 1.
Two nitrates give 2 × 1 = 2.
One Cu matches 2, so copper has valence 2: copper (II).
Answer: copper (II) nitrate.
The numeral goes right after the metal.

Phosphate (PO₄³⁻) has valence 3.
One Fe matches one PO₄, so iron has valence 3.
Answer: iron (III) phosphate.
Phosphide is a single phosphorus atom, not PO₄.

items.text: Which three elements are combined in magnesium carbonate, MgCO₃?
items.why:
Mg is magnesium.
CO₃ gives C (carbon) and O (oxygen).
So the three elements are Mg, C, O.
Ca is calcium, which is not in the formula.

test.why:
Poly means many.
A polyatomic ion is a group of atoms.
The group carries a positive or negative charge.
Answer: a charged group of atoms.

test.text: What is the name of the ion OH⁻?
test.why:
OH⁻ is in Table 3.6, valence 1.
It is one oxygen and one hydrogen with a 1− charge.
Its name is hydroxide.
Oxide is O²⁻, a single atom.

test.text: What is the valence of the sulfate ion SO₄²⁻?
test.why:
The charge on sulfate is 2−.
The valence equals the number of charges.
Answer: 2.
4 is the number of O atoms, not the valence.

test.text: Write the formula of ammonium chloride.
test.why:
Ions: NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻. Valences: 1 and 1.
Criss-cross gives (NH₄)₁Cl₁.
Omit the 1s: NH₄Cl.

test.text: Write the formula of sodium carbonate (Na = 1, CO₃ = 2).
test.why:
Valences: Na 1, CO₃ 2.
Criss-cross: Na takes 2, CO₃ takes 1.
Answer: Na₂CO₃.
Check: 2 × 1 = 2 = 1 × 2.

notes.text: Exercise 3.4 Q1 grid gives Al₂(CO₃)₃ and Fe₂(CO₃)₃ by the valence rule; these are not stable real compounds, so they are not asked.
